absent: Locking, concurrency and calling context for prctl, PSCI, SEV ioctl and PTP ioctls.
Error returns and validation behavior for prctl numbers beyond constant values.
PSCI register calling convention, input parameter layouts and output semantics beyond identifiers and result codes.
SEV platform and guest state machines, command sequencing and side effects beyond command and error enumerations.
PTP device lifecycle, read and poll behavior for events, and hardware effects of pin programming.
Exact ioctl direction and size encoding expansion and compatibility rules between first and second PTP ioctl sets.

findings.text: PowerPC DEXCR prctl interface numbers four hardware aspects from zero upward: speculative branch hint enable is zero, indirect branch recurrent target prediction disable is one, subroutine return address prediction disable is two, and unprivileged hash enable is three.

DEXCR control words use five low bits: editable marker is one, immediate set is two, immediate clear is four, set on next exec is eight, clear on next exec is sixteen, and the combined valid mask is thirty one.

Process shadow stack prctl numbers are seventy four for query, seventy five for update and seventy six for locking; the update mask uses low bit for enable, next bit for write permission and following bit for push permission.

Later prctl numbers pack small suboperations: timer restore identifiers use seventy seven with off zero on one and query two; futex hash uses seventy eight with set slots one and get slots two; restartable sequence slice extension uses seventy nine with get one and set two, where the slice enable value is one.

Control flow integrity prctl numbers are eighty for query and eighty one for update, acting on selector zero for branch landing pads; the update word uses first low bit for enable, second for disable and third for lock.
PSCI call identifiers add a small index to base 0x84000000, while 64-bit calls add further offset 0x40000000 to that base before adding the index.

Assigned PSCI indexes run zero version, one suspend, two off, three on, four affinity, five migrate, six migrate type, seven migrate up cpu, eight system off, nine system reset, ten features, eleven freeze, twelve default suspend, thirteen node state, fourteen system suspend, fifteen suspend mode, sixteen residency, seventeen count, eighteen reset2, nineteen memory protect, twenty protect range check and twenty one off2; only indexes one, three, four, five, seven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, twenty and twenty one have 64-bit forms.

Legacy PSCI power state packs a sixteen bit identifier starting at bit zero, a single type bit at sixteen and a two bit affinity field at twenty four; extended state packs a twenty seven bit identifier starting at bit zero with a single type bit at thirty.

PSCI reports affinity as zero on, one off and two pending; trusted OS topology as zero migratable uniprocessor, one nonmigratable uniprocessor and two multiprocessor; warm reset type is zero with vendor range starting at 0x80000000; hibernate off uses low bit; version packs major in high sixteen and minor in low sixteen; suspend feature exposes power bit at one, initiated flag at zero, with platform coordinated mode zero and OS initiated mode one.

PSCI result codes are zero success, negative one unsupported, negative two invalid parameters, negative three denied, negative four already on, negative five on pending, negative six internal failure, negative seven not present, negative eight disabled and negative nine invalid address.

Secure processor user commands count upward from zero for factory reset, then platform status, key generation, key signing request, Diffie-Hellman generation, certificate export, certificate import, legacy identifier, current identifier, SNP status, SNP commit, SNP configuration and SNP wrapped key load, terminated by a maximum marker.

Secure processor return codes use negative one for no firmware call and zero for success, then hex one through twenty eight for platform and guest faults with gaps where unused values are skipped, an alias equating two spellings of invalid configuration, and later groups at thirty through thirty three and thirty five through three F for buffer sizing, transport and device context faults, terminated by a maximum marker.

Firmware status carrier reports interface major and minor, a state byte, a flag word where bit eight signals encrypted state support, a build byte and a guest count, stored tightly packed without padding.

Key and identifier carriers pass user memory by address plus length: signing request, second identifier query and certificate export use input address with length updated on return, certificate import uses separate addresses with input lengths for platform and owner certificates, and legacy identifier returns two fixed sixty four byte sockets.

SNP status reports interface version and state, a packed flag byte for reverse map initialization, build identifier, a packed feature word for chip identifier masking, chip key masking, virtual key enable, feature info, power limit disable and ciphertext hiding capability and enable, plus guest count and two version counters; companion configuration carries reported version with masking bits and reserved space; wrapped key load carries length, version, padding and address; hash stick is a fixed four hundred thirty two byte blob.
Command envelope is tightly packed holding a thirty two bit selector, a sixty four bit user pointer and a thirty two bit error output.
Single secure processor user entry is a read-write ioctl numbered zero under type S operating on that envelope to dispatch any command number.

Precision clock flags use low bits for enable, rising edge, falling edge, strict validation and extended offset, with combined valid masks for current and first version external timestamp and periodic output, plus single shot, duty cycle and phase bits for periodic output and enable-only validity for events.

Clock time is signed seconds plus nanoseconds with spare; capabilities report adjustment limits, counts of alarms, timestamp channels, outputs and pins, plus support flags for pulse, cross timestamping and phase tune with reserved tail; external timestamp request selects channel with flag word; periodic output selects start or phase by flag, period with zero meaning disable, channel and either on duration or spare.

Offset measurement allows up to twenty five samples, with classic form interleaving system and device stamps ending in system time, extended form pairing per sample stamps under a clock identifier, and precise form returning device plus realtime and monotonic raw stamps; pin descriptor carries sixty four byte name, pin index, function selector among none, external timestamp, periodic output and physical sync, channel and spare; event report carries timestamp, channel, type and spare.

Precision clock device uses magic equals with numbers one through twenty two for capability query, external timestamp and periodic output setup, pulse enable, three offset queries, pin query and program, duplicate second set, mask clear and single enable, and cycle based precise and extended offset queries.

Secure structures distinguish input address and length from kernel filled outputs, with lengths updated on return and reserved bytes left zero; all secure envelopes and status carriers are packed with no implicit padding.

Precision clock requests gate union members by flags, treat zero period as disable, require on time below period, bound pin numbers by capability count, bind pin channels to request indexes, limit samples to twenty five, and preserve reserved words for future use.

User supplied sixty four bit addresses with separate lengths for keys, certificates, identifiers and command payloads require bounds and access validation, since kernel reads inputs and writes outputs through them with length feedback; ioctl selector must be range checked against maximum marker.

Sample count above twenty five or channel and pin indexes beyond reported counts would overflow fixed arrays or misdirect hardware; flag words must be masked against valid sets with version specific subsets.
